why:
D11 / PI-20260927-EPMBGUYB-0003 -- root-cause and fix operator-owed-guard's intermittent age reads. Tier-1 by TIER1_SURFACE: the whole diff is scripts/ci/check_operator_owed.py (scripts/ci/**), tests/test_operator_owed.py (tests/**), plus this branch's own landing paperwork under .github/** (the decl file is excluded from LANDING_MACHINERY by check_pr_landing.py's own `p != decl_rel` clause). NO src/, NO config/, NO deploy/, no unit file, no order path, no workflow YAML change needed -- fetch-depth was already 0 (see below).

THE BUG: docs/plans/review-pack-2026-09-27.md documents `operator-owed-guard` reading 4 specific pipeline rows (OI-20260913-A-BYBIT2-HEDGE-BOOK-..., PI-20260924-MQ3CDMU6-0001/0002, PI-20260924-GIGNEYV1-0001) as age >= 2.0 days on the `guards` CI runs at 07:39-07:43Z for PRs #13084/#13091 today, while a LATER local run of the identical check on the same/newer commit read the same rows as 1.3 days -- described in that doc as 'time-sensitive in a way that does not track simple wall-clock elapsed time 1:1'.

CANDIDATES CHECKED AGAINST THE CODE, NOT ASSUMED: (a) naive/aware timezone confusion -- RULED OUT. Every timestamp on this path is aware: `_dt.datetime.now(_dt.timezone.utc)` in both check_operator_owed.py and scripts/ops/pipeline.py::is_due, and git's `%cI` always carries an explicit offset which `datetime.fromisoformat` parses correctly; Python's aware-datetime subtraction is correct across differing offsets (verified directly: commits recorded in both +03:00 and +00:00 in the same window convert to identical, correct UTC instants). (b) a shallow clone / fetch-depth -- RULED OUT. Grepped every `.github/workflows/*.yml` for `check_operator_owed`: `check_operator_owed.py` is invoked from exactly one place, the `operator-owed-guard` entry in `scripts/ci/run_guards.py`, run by `.github/workflows/guards.yml`'s single `guards` job, whose checkout step is `fetch-depth: 0` (full history) -- confirmed by reading that workflow directly.

THE CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE: `record_ages()` computed a row's 'content age' from the git COMMITTER date of the commit that merged its record file into `main` (`git log -1 --format=%cI`) -- i.e. whenever this repo's serialized self-land merge queue (scripts/ops/claim_merge_slot.py, one claimant at a time) happened to free that PR's slot -- and NOT from when the record was actually written. MEASURED directly against the live register (docs/claude/work/pipeline/), over the 110 most recent non-migration record files: every one (0/110) lands at or after its own filename timestamp (never before, as expected), median gap 35.6 minutes, mean 107.6 minutes, max ~27.9 hours, and 98/110 (89%) exceed 10 minutes. Concretely reproduced for the exact 4 rows named above: their newest generations (filenames timestamped 08:31:42Z-09:08:16Z on 2026-09-27) landed via PR #13096, whose merge commit's committer date is 08:55:56Z -- i.e. a row authored at 08:31:42Z did not exist in `main`'s content at all until nearly 25 minutes later, and any earlier check (such as the 07:39-07:43Z CI run, which necessarily predates that merge) correctly saw the row's PRIOR, older generation as current -- reading it as stale exactly as designed, not in error. The APPARENT instability is that once the row's committer-date-based age is read at all, it tracks *time since this PR's merge-queue slot freed*, a value that moves with queue congestion rather than with the row's own history, so two reads taken on opposite sides of an in-flight merge can legitimately disagree by far more than their own wall-clock gap.

THE FIX: `record_ages()` now prefers the record's OWN authoring timestamp -- embedded in its filename by `pipeline._record_filename()` (`{YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSffffff}Z-{rand}.json`), a plain `datetime.now(UTC)` read at write time and never touched again -- and asks git for a date only when that timestamp cannot be parsed (the legacy flat-file store's `line N` sources). This makes 'age' immune to how long a row's carrying PR sat in the merge queue: the filename is fixed at write time regardless of when git happens to see it.

VERIFICATION: all 41 existing tests in tests/test_operator_owed.py pass unchanged (the old git-log-backed fixtures use synthetic filenames like `0000-ID.json` that do not match the new timestamp regex, so they fall back to the prior git-log path exactly as before -- nothing about the existing behavior for the legacy/fixture shape changed). A new pinning test, test_record_ages_reads_the_records_own_filename_timestamp_not_the_landing_commit, reproduces the exact failure shape (a record filename-timestamped 10 minutes old, landed via a commit backdated 30 days) and was confirmed to FAIL pre-fix (read 30.0 days) and PASS post-fix (reads <1.0 day) by stashing the src change, re-running, and restoring it. The guard's own `--self-test` (14 planted controls) also still passes unchanged. `python3 scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py --branch <this branch> --base origin/main` passes locally (see PR body / CI). No parameter, roster, config or order-path value is changed; this is a pure measurement-correctness fix to a CI guard.
